sprint: From This World -- Wrapping Grid + Images/Graphics Category Grouping
task: Item #5 of a new six-item governing request: 'Change look of from this world. we have enough space. maximize space usage so maximum assets can be seen at a time.' Plus item #6's own literal wording, 'Under add category for images', folded into the same pass since both target js/contextPanel.js's Collection From This World browsing picker. The picker's existing implementation was a fixed-height, overflow-x:auto horizontal scroll strip mirroring js/objectStrip.js's own scroll-strip pattern -- the right tradeoff for the Object Strip (bounded height beside a fixed canvas) but the wrong call for a browse-everything picker, which was trading away visible real estate for a constant small height. Rewritten as a wrapping, auto-fill CSS grid mirroring Sticker Studio's own .sticker-studio-grid pattern (repeat(auto-fill,minmax(96px,1fr))), filling the full sidebar width and wrapping into as many rows as needed, relying on .right-sidebar's own pre-existing overflow-y:auto as the only scroll mechanism -- no per-picker scroll container or arrow buttons at all. Entries are grouped into two labelled sections, Images (N) and Graphics (N), confirmed via grep that registerCollectionAsset() only ever produces these two kind values; an empty group is never shown. Old dead scroll-strip CSS removed outright; new .context-collection-group-label + rewritten .context-collection-picker-grid/.context-collection-tile added. _addCollectionObject/_activeCollectionAssets unchanged -- only the picker's rendering function and CSS changed. Verified via a new 19-assertion Playwright suite (superseding the now-obsolete horizontal-scroll-strip test) across two scenarios: a small 2-image/0-graphic theme confirming exactly one non-empty group label and a genuine auto-fill grid (verified against the AUTHORED CSS rule text, not computed style, since getComputedStyle always resolves repeat(auto-fill,...) to concrete pixel tracks in every browser); and a large 12-image/6-graphic theme confirming the decisive proof -- tiles genuinely wrap into multiple visible rows rather than being confined to one scrolling strip. Full regression across 6 sibling scratch suites sharing contextPanel.js/style.css all pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to js/contextPanel.js and css/style.css.
